text:
jamie: fyi i'm hitting a reproducible hang in the go sample that wraps generator streaming + token refresh. thought i'd dump notes here before opening a bug report.

jamie: short repro: start a generator stream, mid-stream rotate auth by calling stream.UpdateBearer(newTok), then cancel the ctx from the caller. caller returns immediately but process shows goroutine stuck in UpdateBearer until remote handshake completes.

jamie: snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for t := range tokStream {
    iter.UpdateBearer(t)
  }
}()
// cancel after first chunk
cancel()
// caller exits but iter goroutine still alive
```

rao: that sounds like UpdateBearer is doing a blocking RPC or grabbing a mutex that waits on network IO. ctx cancel doesn't help if the internal code isn't using the ctx.

nina: is the hang visible on the server side as an open websocket? or do we just see a goroutine leak client-side?

jamie: client-side goroutine leak, underlying TCP still open for ~20-40s. in a local debug run i could see UpdateBearer waiting on a response from the runtime.

sam: two directions: (A) change UpdateBearer to be atomic/nonblocking (swap token pointer + notify send loop), (B) accept a context into UpdateBearer so callers can cancel the auth handshake. both have tradeoffs.

lucy: +1 for atomic swap. semantics: UpdateBearer should never block caller's cancellation. The send loop will pick up latest token on next send. If we need immediate reauth and to surface errors, provide a separate Reauth(ctx) that can block and return errors.

rao: another option: stream.CloseWithContext(ctx) or ForceClose() that immediately tears down connection regardless of in-flight auth. That matches user expectation that ctx cancel is a hard stop.

nina: ergonomics note: many users will do the naive pattern of spinning a goroutine that UpdateBearer for each refresh. If UpdateBearer blocks, a single slow refresh can cascade. docs should warn, but SDK should do the safe default.

jamie: agreed. i'm preparing two patches: (1) make UpdateBearer do pointer swap + channel notify, nonblocking, and (2) add StreamHandle.CloseNow() which forcibly closes transport. will gate CloseNow under a method on the returned handle so it's opt-in.

sam: please also add a Stream.Done() channel or Done() method so callers can select on it. i.e. iter.Done() that closes when the stream resources fully released. that makes it easy to ensure background goroutines aren't left.

lucy: +1. pattern: iter, errCh := client.Gen.StreamV2(ctx, req) or iter := client.Gen.StreamV2(ctx, req) where iter.Done() returns <-chan struct{}. keep naming conservative though.

infra-bot: note: if you prefix the PR with "devex/stream-cancel" we'll add runtime and devex reviewers automatically.

jamie: i'll add a tiny example under examples/stream-cancel that reproduces the token-rotate + cancel sequence and asserts that no goroutines remain after Done() closes.

rao: small implementation detail: ensure UpdateBearer swap is atomic and doesn't cause the send goroutine to attempt a mid-payload header rewrite. best to apply token at chunk boundary.

nina: also consider using per-request auth headers rather than mutating connection-level auth mid-stream. that complicates resumable streams but is simpler for short-lived tokens.

jamie: good point. for long-running streams where you must rotate, nonblocking swap + send-loop pick-up + optional Reauth(ctx) for synchronous failure reporting covers most cases.

sam: when you open the PR, please include a CHANGELOG entry and a short snippet in the onboarding guide: "Interrupting a stream: cancel the ctx, wait on iter.Done(), or call iter.CloseNow() if you need immediate teardown."

lucy: one more: add a small test that simulates the server delaying handshake response to ensure CloseNow actually aborts any blocked operations (helps runtime folks spot kernel-level issues).

jamie: thanks — i'll prototype and post the PR link here. happy to pair with runtime on the test that injects a delayed handshake.

infra-bot: reminder: we try to land devex API compatibility changes behind StreamV2 for GA parity. check with PM if we need to ship a compat wrapper.

jamie: noted. planning StreamV2 and a compat shim Stream that uses the old behavior.

sam: this should reduce a ton of the "generator hangs after ctrl-c" tickets.

jamie: fine. will follow up with PR and examples.
